record.change: hardware-assisted IEEE CRC32 in the upload benchmark consumer
record.reason: Final three rotated checksum pairs measure median 25.78 us/MiB for the Zig port versus 25.95 for Go; original Zig std.hash.Crc32 cost 1706.58. Exact results independently verified with zlib. Preserve incremental and portable paths and Go BSD attribution. HTTP core has no CRC work.

record.change: combine the final fixed-length body consumer and response handler task
record.reason: Three early pairs favor the change but include placement noise. Controlled confirmation using the same old cache and application CPU reduces 64 KiB CPU from 684.59 to 665.83 us/MiB (2.7%), with unchanged throughput and p99. Incremental effect is not isolated on the final cache. Keep absolute deadline recheck between callbacks; chunked finalization still follows complete terminal framing.

Controlled pair: 64 KiB CPU 666.31 to 666.15 us/MiB; 8 MiB saturated 327.90 to 335.07, unchanged link-limited throughput. Paced CPU improved in an exploratory comparison but no overall repeatable benefit established. Reverted both worker and diagnostic metrics from the saved preceding snapshot.

record.change: coalesce completion eventfd notifications on empty queue transitions
record.reason: Two rotated pairs per size: no material throughput, tail, or CPU improvement over finalization. Restore worker from before-notify; retain independent CRC style and build-test changes.

record.change: poll eventfd readiness and drain on network worker
record.reason: 64 KiB paired CPU 665.74 to 661.17 us/MiB; 8 MiB saturated 325.77 to 323.29. Differences below 1%; no material throughput change. Paced still above Go. Full component and affected wire suites passed, but no overall measurable benefit.

record.change: combine ring submission and completion waiting
record.reason: Fewer ring-entry calls in traced serial uploads, but controlled 64 KiB CPU 668.07 to 665.29 us/MiB, unchanged throughput and tail. Single 8 MiB pair improved 328.89 to 321.48 us/MiB; insufficient overall evidence to retain over the previous implementation. Full component and streaming/executor suites passed.

record.change: unlock the application task queue before signaling a consumer
record.reason: Two rotated pairs at each body size showed no material throughput or CPU benefit. 64 KiB CPU remained about 666 us/MiB, and 8 MiB CPU about 323-331 us/MiB. Full component and streaming/executor tests passed. Restore the last retained finalization implementation.

record.change: retain burst-sized small-buffer caches with a byte bound
record.reason: Three natural rotated pairs reduce median CPU from 688.10 to 317.05 us/MiB, with unchanged ~279.4 MiB/s. All candidate measurement windows have zero buffer allocations and minor faults. Calibrated pair reduces CPU 698.73 to 269.89 us/MiB. Preserve 8-block allowance for large buffers; cap smaller caches at 64 blocks within 4 MiB per size class. New unchanged wire regression fails before (112 allocations vs 64) and passes after.
Wait for the active comparison group to finish, then test the observed large-buffer allocation churn.
